answer: A published nullifier on each registration bond means one deposit can back only one seat. To register, a seat locks 2,000 POA and publishes a nullifier, the hash of that deposit's output, on the shared ledger; any other seat citing the same nullifier is refused by every node. The bond stays locked for 30 epochs and is slashed in full if graders prove the seat is a clone. So 100 fakes need 200,000 POA locked at once, with no lending or reuse between them, while an honest seat posts one bond and works, whether it issues gale warnings, surveys a cliff ledge or prices velvet stock.
